equations.audit: L explicitly negative log likelihood yet RHS is minus expected Hessian; under regular likelihood identity negative log likelihood requires plus. Scalar unit-variance Gaussian NLL has Hessian1, so printed RHS−1 cannot equal Fisher1. Implementation not inspected.
target gradients require target labels and a specified loss; adaptation versus evaluation labels not separated explicitly

equations.function: compare source-model Fisher on source and target
equations.audit: general PSD product-root convention and regularity not specified; subsequent diagonal reduction avoids noncommutativity issue. Source-model-conditioned score need not be symmetric across retrained tasks.

first line norm; expanded second line lacks squared element differences before summation. Literal expression can be imaginary and is not the norm. Claimed[0,1] incompatible with F2 y-axis reaching25 unless unreported scale/normalization differs.

equations.audit: G definition repeats weekday indicator on both terms, rather than distinct weekday/weekend terms; time coordinate units and recursive generation not fully specified

statistics.analysis_units: source-target tasks for association; region-year queries and households for transfer; data points temporally dependent
statistics.independent_n: not established; five queries share source library and households share dataset;10repeats not10independentdatasets
statistics.leakage_risk: empirical target Fisher requires labeled examples; unclear whether source selection, adaptation, and scoring use disjoint chronological samples. This is protocol uncertainty, not proven leakage.
statistics.fairness: few target epochs demonstrates initialization utility under that budget, not globally superior architecture or total-compute efficiency
statistics.ablation_note: nearest versus second-nearest is rank contrast; random initialization changes prior training as well as selection, so cannot isolate TAS versus generic transfer

numeric_checks.boundary: printed-cell arithmetic only; not raw data replication;prose32%estimator unresolved

claims_and_logic.claim: TAS is a theoretically sound task similarity measure
claims_and_logic.assessment: mechanism plausible as diagonal Fisher distance but printed algebra and plotted scale are inconsistent; empirical synthetic order not proof
few-epoch performance evidence; no wall-clock/end-to-end cost proof
mostly positive reported comparisons with QLD03exceptions andRMSEfine-tuningtrade-off
no modern transfer benchmark suite executed; random-init comparisons cannot establish broad transfer-method superiority

conclusions.supported: source-conditioned selection and limited-epoch transfer show useful reported behavior on two Australian datasets and synthetic tasks
limits: not universal avoidance of negative transfer
conclusions.future_work: TAS-guided subset selection within MAML/T-MAML is proposed, not implemented

language.narrative: application need→source-selection gap→mathematical proxy→synthetic mechanism check→two empirical datasets→future meta-learning
cautions: empirical proof conflates evidence with proof
significantly and superiority exceed reported inferential tests
conclusion says traditional transfer approaches despite weak baseline diversity
source and query indices/roles should remain stable
original_functional_frames: A source-selection score should be evaluated separately from the benefits of pretraining itself.
Under a fixed adaptation budget, report both successful transfer and target domains showing negative transfer.
Efficiency claims should include source-library construction and selection overhead, not only fine-tuning epochs.
